descriptions.text: On June 2, Bitcoin flash-crashed on a major Bitcoin trading platform Kraken. The near vertical drop from $11,200 CAD to $100 CAD within moments initially appeared to have resulted from a technical glitch or a fat-fingered trading error by a whale. In this case, the available evidence suggests a hacker compromised a whale’s account, stole 1200 BTC worth $10.45 million on that date, and then dumped this huge amount of BTC into a highly illiquid BTC/CAD marke.

Kraken’s BTC/CAD market flash-crashed on 2019-06-02 after a suspected account compromise, with public reports tying the incident to about 1,200 BTC and roughly $10.45 million in reported loss. The public record points to a compromised Kraken account and a very thin BTC/CAD order book that let an attacker convert customer BTC into fills on an attacker-controlled account at a sharply distorted price. The exact compromise path into the account, and any exchange-side reversal or recovery action, are not independently confirmed.
